properties.name: AMEC Building
properties.description: African M.E. church building tied to the Clayborn Temple congregation and the 1968 sanitation workers' organizing.

properties.name: Aretha Franklin Birth Home
properties.description: Birthplace of the Queen of Soul, Aretha Franklin, born in this South Memphis home in 1942.
properties.photoCredit: WillyBearden, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Cornelia Crenshaw Memorial Library
properties.description: Public library named for civil rights activist Cornelia Crenshaw, a key supporter of the 1968 sanitation workers' strike.

properties.name: First Baptist Beale (Ida B. Wells Office)
properties.description: Historic Beale Street church that housed the newspaper office of journalist and anti-lynching crusader Ida B. Wells.
properties.photoCredit: John Phelan, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

nrhp.note: Listed as Beale Street Baptist Church.

properties.name: Grigg's Business and Practical Arts College
properties.description: One of Memphis's Black business and vocational colleges, serving the community through the segregation era.
properties.photoCredit: Dclemens1971, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Historic Clayborn Temple
properties.description: Rallying point and headquarters for the 1968 sanitation workers' strike, birthplace of the 'I AM A MAN' banners.
properties.photoCredit: Jayhedges24, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

nrhp.note: Listed as Second Presbyterian Church; raised to national significance under the name Clayborn Temple in 2017.

properties.name: LeMoyne-Owen College
properties.description: Historically Black college with roots to 1862, long a center of Black education and civil rights activism in Memphis.
properties.photoCredit: Dclemens1971, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Lorraine Motel / National Civil Rights Museum
properties.description: Site of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination in 1968, now the National Civil Rights Museum.
properties.photoCredit: Matthew T Rader, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

nrhp.note: Listed as a contributing property of the South Main Street Historic District, not on its own.

properties.name: Mason Temple
properties.description: World headquarters of the Church of God in Christ, where Dr. King gave his final 'Mountaintop' speech in 1968.
properties.photoCredit: Jim Roberts, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: NAACP Memphis Headquarters
properties.description: Longtime home of the Memphis branch of the NAACP.

properties.name: Old Daisy Theater
properties.description: Historic 1917 Beale Street movie house, an entertainment anchor of Black Memphis.
properties.photoCredit: Sallyelaine444, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Orpheum Theatre Balcony Project
properties.description: Grand 1928 theatre near Beale Street; the Balcony Project reckons with its segregated past.
properties.photoCredit: Bjoertvedt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: People's Grocery
properties.street: Walker Ave & Mississippi Blvd, Memphis, TN 38106
properties.description: Site of the 1892 lynching at 'the Curve' that launched Ida B. Wells's national anti-lynching campaign.
properties.photoCredit: Photographer unknown, c.1890, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: R.S. Lewis Funeral Home
properties.description: Black-owned funeral home that provided the hearse for Dr. King and supported the civil rights movement.
properties.photoCredit: Magnolia677, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Robert R. Church Auditorium
properties.description: Auditorium in Church Park, built by Robert R. Church Sr., the South's first Black millionaire.
properties.photoCredit: Thomas R Machnitzki, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Robert R. Church Home
properties.description: Home site associated with Robert R. Church, pioneering Black businessman and civic leader.

properties.name: Rock 'n' Soul Museum + Hall of Fame
properties.description: Smithsonian-affiliated museum telling the story of Memphis music and the people who made it.
properties.photoCredit: Gary J. Wood, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Royal Studios
properties.description: One of the oldest continuously operating recording studios, home of Hi Records and Al Green's soul sound.
properties.photoCredit: Thomas R Machnitzki, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Stax / Soulsville Foundation Campus
properties.description: Site of Stax Records, birthplace of Memphis soul, now the Stax Museum and Soulsville campus.
properties.photoCredit: Avalon Frost, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Universal Life Building
properties.street: 480 Dr Martin Luther King Jr Ave, Memphis, TN 38126
properties.description: Landmark home of Universal Life Insurance, a cornerstone of Black economic power in Memphis.
properties.photoCredit: Spencer Kellum, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

properties.name: Withers Collection Museum & Gallery
properties.description: Gallery of photographer Ernest Withers, who documented the civil rights movement and Memphis music.

properties.name: Club Paradise / The Soul Train Lounge
properties.description: Legendary Memphis music venue that hosted soul and blues greats.

properties.name: Lewis Park / Martin Stadium
properties.description: Park and former Martin Stadium, home of the Memphis Red Sox of the Negro Leagues.

properties.name: Memphis Slim House
properties.description: Restored home of blues pianist Memphis Slim, now a collaboratory for local musicians.
